Subject: Clarify marketplace listing rebilling and renewal billing policy

Team —

Quick one: AWS rep asked whether listing credits we received last year (the Q1 co-marketing/listing credit) will be rebilled to us as part of the renewal if we change tiers during the term. They used the phrase "rebilling on change-of-tier / mid-term reconciliation." I want to make sure we know the accounting and procurement ask before I escalate.

Specifically I need:
- Is a credit applied as a line-item credit on invoice or as an upfront rebate?
- If we switch to Reserved/Dedicated capacity mid-quarter, do credits reflow and create a chargeback?
- Any PO/invoice actions we must take to avoid surprise hits to committed spend?

I've attached the AWS credit agreement we signed last Feb and the GCP Day-1 statement for reference. Can you each flag anything I should call out to the partner (fees that typically get rebilled, common doc requests they ask for)?

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace listing rebilling and renewal billing policy

Hi Monica —

Thanks for sending the agreement. Short answer: credits are applied per the credit instrument terms. In our typical AWS Marketplace listing program we treat most listing/marketing credits as contra-invoice items in the billing period they are reconciled. That means:

- If a credit was issued as a quarterly contra invoice and you change tiers mid-quarter, the credit will be reconciled in the quarter where the usage occurs.
- We do offer an exception process for customers moving from pay-as-you-go to reserved commitments mid-term — engineering charges are prorated, but the partner operations team may require a short reconciliation.
- For avoid surprises, provide the PO that references the committed USD spend and flag the marketplace credits on the PO. That prevents automated rebilling against those credits.

I'll pull the exact clause in your credit instrument and confirm whether your paperwork triggers an automatic reflow. If you can confirm your committed start date for Dedicated (do you have a final SOW?), I can model the reconciliation.

Best,
Alexa Barnes
Partner Programs, AWS Marketplace

Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace listing rebilling and renewal billing policy

Monica / Alexa —

Couple of notes from finance procurement side:
1) Our standard PO templates explicitly call out marketplace credits as a separate line item. When procurement issues the PO we will add a note: "Credits issued prior to PO effective date shall not be rebilled unless explicitly stated in vendor credit terms." That has worked with other marketplaces.
2) If the partner treats credits as contra-invoice, we typically need the partner to provide a credit memo referencing the original invoice(s) so our AP system can net it out.
3) For reserved capacity moves: we treat the new commitment as a new contract start; any credits tied to the prior contract are handled by reconciliation and should not auto-apply to the new commitment unless the credit instrument language says so.

Action items for Monica: please confirm the Dedicated start date and upload the final SOW. I've flagged AP to expect a credit memo request from AWS if Alexa confirms contra-invoice.

— Marissa
Director, Finance Ops

On Wed, Mar 7, 2028 at 3:30 PM Alexa Barnes <alexa.barnes@aws-partners.com> wrote:

Monica / Marissa — quick follow up after legal reviewed the instrument. Two important clarifications:

1) Contract clause 3.4 (Credit Application) says credits issued as "promotional listing credits" are not refundable and will be applied only against Marketplace usage invoices tied to the named entity. If the named entity changes accounting structure (e.g., new billing account for Reserved capacity), credits will be flagged for manual reconciliation and are not automatically re-assigned.

2) We can issue a one-time credit memo to offset any automatic rebilling if you provide the PO referencing the new commitment and the original credit reference numbers.

Next steps I can do from AWS side: prepare a sample credit memo and a short reconciliation worksheet. If you can confirm the Dedicated start date and the billing account ID, I'll generate the memo and coordinate with our AP.

Regards,
Alexa
